channel.title: Battery Sensei
channel.description: Updates for Battery Sensei — a quiet macOS menu-bar battery utility.

item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
1.0

Battery Sensei is the menu-bar battery utility I wanted but couldn't find. One that knows my calendar.

It reads your next four hours of meetings and warns you before your battery dies during one. At -30, -15, -5, or -1 minutes. You pick. Event titles never leave your Mac.

It also does the usual: charge cap with weekly recalibration, per-app battery use over the last hour / day / week, and a soft history strip so you can see what your battery has been through.

Five languages. macOS 14 or later. Apple Silicon or Intel.

Drag it into Applications.

item.title: Version 1.1.0
item.description:
1.1

Sharper meeting alerts and a real Settings window.

You now pick exactly which checkpoints fire before each meeting: -30, -15, -5, -1. Default is -30 and -5. The toggle chips match the website. Changes apply the moment you flip them.

The Settings window stops vanishing when you click another app. (It used to. Sorry.)

Other small things:

  • "Latest forecast" stays put when no meeting needs warning about. Empty state reads "No conflicts" instead of disappearing.
  • Hover states on snooze buttons and reminder chips, finally.
  • "Show event titles" replaces "Hide event titles". Default is on.
  • Live "N min left" countdown actually counts down now.

item.title: Version 1.1.1
item.description:
1.1.1

Sparkle now downloads and installs updates silently. You won't see another "Install update?" prompt unless you opt out in the dialog.

Two layout fixes: the Activate Pro button matches the Buy button's height again, and the Latest forecast card aligns to one column instead of three.

item.title: Version 1.2.0
item.description:
1.2

One-click activation after you buy.

Click "Open Sensei & activate" on the thank-you page and the app opens with your license key already typed in. You click Activate. That's it. No more copy-paste from the email.

Also: the in-app Buy button now drops you straight into the checkout flow instead of bouncing through the marketing page.

item.title: Version 1.2.1
item.description:
1.2.1

Two reliability fixes.

The "Install and Relaunch" window now actually comes to the front when Sparkle has an update ready. Previously the app was a menu-bar accessory and the prompt could be born behind whatever you were doing.

Activating a new license no longer risks leaving you locked out. The new key gets activated first; the old one only releases if the new one succeeds. Network blip, typo, cancelled mid-flow — your existing license stays put. The sheet now shows a small warning when you're about to swap.

item.title: Version 1.2.2
item.description:
1.2.2

Settings polish.

The settings window no longer floats above other apps' full-screen Spaces. Standard window ordering applies: click the full-screen app behind it and the settings drops behind, like every other Mac window.

The menu-bar display picker (Percent / Time / Icon) got a once-over. All three battery glyphs are now the same width regardless of which mode you pick. The selected tile is outlined in red in light mode and white in dark mode — border only, no background fill, so the preview strip behind reads through.

Manage and Run Setup Wizard Again lost their trailing dots, along with Settings, Share image, Activate Pro, Check for Updates, and Check now. Cleaner action labels across the app.

License section: Manage Subscription is now a proper accent link with hover, matching how Manage Activations already looks in the activation sheet. Remove from this Mac stays a bordered button — destructive actions earn deliberate buttons.

Activating a different license key no longer risks locking you out. The new key is activated first; the old one only releases if that succeeds. Failed network, typo, sheet cancellation — your existing license stays put. The activation sheet shows a small warning banner when you're about to swap so you know what's happening.

item.title: Version 1.2.3
item.description:
1.2.3

Quieter idle, sharper feedback.

Battery Sensei now does noticeably less work when nothing's happening. The menu-bar charging pulse runs at half the previous rate (still reads as motion, half the redraws), the icon render cache holds 4× more entries so the percent/time display stops thrashing, and the meeting forecast only re-publishes when the predicted severity actually changes. A few CPU hot spots in the per-app history store got cleaned up too.

Hover affordances filled in across the app. Every interactive surface, including the warning-mode wizard cards, the language picker, the saga search clear button, and the rescue-receipt dismiss, now responds to pointer-over with a subtle scale lift and pointing-hand cursor. Six gaps closed.

Removing a license from this Mac now asks first. Confirmation dialog explains the slot returns to your pool, and the destructive button is clearly labeled. Hover on the button is consistent with the Manage link beside it.

The settings window stops floating above other apps' full-screen Spaces. Click a full-screen app behind it and the settings drops behind, like every other Mac window.

A few visual fit-and-finish bits: the Lifetime badge corner radius now matches the Remove button beside it, the hero card kanji watermark lights red on hover like all the other cards, and the menu-bar icon picker has a uniform battery glyph width across Percent / Time / Icon.

item.title: Version 1.2.4
item.description:
1.2.4

Lighter idle, sharper history, calmer meeting alerts.

The per-app history store no longer blocks the main thread on every sample tick. JSON re-encodes and disk writes now run on a background queue and coalesce back-to-back saves into a single write — the sampler itself returns instantly. Top-app aggregations are memoized inside each tick so the same window query never re-runs the filter, group, and battery-attribution pass twice. A battery app shouldn't drain battery; it now drains noticeably less.

The Saga charge history chart got a hover crosshair. Scrub the line and a pinned tooltip shows the timestamp and exact percentage of the nearest sample, anchored to the chart bounds so it never clips off-screen. Tap-away clears it. The annotation snaps to real readings instead of interpolating between them.

Meeting battery alerts dropped the redundant "Meeting battery guard" kicker. The calendar hero already establishes context and the sentence already names the event, so the alert now leads straight with the prediction at hero typography. Line spacing widens on the more urgent surfaces so multi-clause predictions stay readable when they wrap.

Removing a license from this Mac and swapping in a new key now both prompt with clear consequences. The deactivate dialog explains the activation slot returns to your pool. Activating a new key when one is already on the Mac warns that the existing license stays put if the new one fails or you cancel — no silent overwrite.

First-run calendar guard surface gained a one-line hint pointing at the master switch up top, so the empty state doesn't read as broken before you've enabled monitoring.

item.title: Version 1.2.5
item.description:
1.2.5

Per-app energy chart and ranking, fixed.

The 24-hour and 7-day per-app charts now downsample. Previously every 5-minute sample landed as its own point, so the curve was a fuzzy band on the day view (≈288 points) and visual noise on the week view (≈2016 points). Buckets are anchored to the chart's visible window — 24h collapses to ~30-minute averages, 7d to ~3-hour averages — and a freshly-installed app with only 30 minutes of samples now occupies one bucket at the right time position instead of stacking five dots on top of each other at the right edge. The 1-hour view stays raw. PointMarks removed from the per-app chart; the line alone reads cleanly.

Row ordering matches the displayed number. The top-apps list now sorts by estimated battery percent — the value actually printed under each app name — instead of the per-sample energy impact score. Previously a row reading "238% in the last 7 days" could appear below a row reading "34%" because their internal impact scores ran the other way. On Intel Macs (no battery attribution), the ranking falls back to energy impact as before.

24-hour and 7-day views now exclude apps that weren't observed for most of the window. An app whose earliest sample lands more than 10% into the window — 2.4h on the day view, 16.8h on the week view — was either recently installed or only started running late, and its battery share isn't comparable to apps that ran the whole time. The 1-hour view keeps all apps visible so fresh-launch UX still has something to show on the first tick.

item.title: Version 1.2.6
item.description:
1.2.6

Calmer home, quieter window chrome, redesigned rescue receipt.

The Pro / Trial home badge dropped its card chrome. The licensed and trial states now sit as an inline strip with just the Pro pill on the left and the Manage link on the right, no box around them. Previous attempts to match the box to the hero card below kept reading as slightly misaligned — narrower, wider, or floating on a different plane. As a top utility strip the row stops competing with the hero card directly underneath.

Card surfaces are now fully opaque. Light and dark themes both used to render cards at 94–98% opacity, which let the window-wide washi parchment patina bleed through onto card backgrounds. The intent was a subtle paper texture; the effect was the background overlapping the cards. Cards now have a clean ground; the washi texture stays visible in the gutters between cards where it belongs.

The window's top chrome strip no longer leaves a visible seam. The old mask held full opacity for the first half then ramped to clear, which produced a faint horizontal line across the window — and the macOS rounded window corners pinched that line asymmetrically, making the corners look broken. A pure linear falloff dissolves the chrome into the parchment with no detectable boundary.

The Battery Rescue Receipt sheet got the full zen pass:

  • A hanko stamp glyph (concentric hinomaru rings around a checkmark seal) replaces the bolt-heart-in-warning-circle. Reads as stamped / approved, matches the receipt metaphor.
  • A 印 ("seal") kanji watermark sits at top-trailing at paper-faint opacity, matching the watermark pattern used on the rest of the saga cards.
  • The receipt body sits in an inner tinted-and-bordered panel so the summary reads as the stamped content of the receipt, not another paragraph on the card. A hairline washi divider separates the header from the body like a tear line.
  • The outer card gained the saga card vocabulary — ZenRadius.xl, theme border stroke, soft shadow — so the sheet sits at the same elevation as its neighbours instead of looking like a flat sub-element.
  • All three actions now lead with icons: Copy (filled doc), Share (system arrow-up-square), Not Now (xmark). The dismiss option previously read as inert text; with the same icon-leading vocabulary as its peers it reads as a peer control, just visually subordinate.
  • Hover scale lift added to every button.

item.title: Version 1.2.7
item.description:
1.2.7

Rescue receipt redesigned, copy quieted.

The Battery Rescue Receipt sheet got the full zen pass. A hanko stamp glyph — concentric hinomaru rings around a checkmark seal — replaces the bolt-heart-in-warning-circle hero. A 印 ("seal") kanji sits as a paper-faint watermark in the top corner. The receipt body now reads as a real receipt: two stat tiles for the saved-at percentage and the time-remaining estimate, then a hinomaru-tinted outcome strip below them — the equivalent of a "PAID" stamp on paper. A hairline washi divider separates the header from the body like a tear line.

The Not Now button stopped looking like inert text. It's now a real bordered button with the same icon-leading vocabulary as Copy and Share (xmark glyph), an inline "Esc" keycap so the keyboard shortcut is discoverable on the surface itself, and Esc actually dismisses the sheet now via the standard cancel-action binding.

The copy across every language stepped away from the marketing-deck register. "Sensei intervention: successful. Copy or share the receipt when the save is too dramatic to keep private." became "A small moment worth keeping. Copy or share if you'd like." The receipt summary dropped its redundant "intervention: successful" tail. The outcome strip carries a single word — "Saved." in English, "Gerettet." in German, "A salvo." in Spanish, "Sauvé." in French, "救えた。" in Japanese — beside the seal stamp. Title shortened in English and German ("Rescue Receipt", "Rettungsbeleg") so it doesn't repeat "Battery". The kicker above the title carries the rescue timestamp now ("印 · 28 May 14:20"), not a duplicate of the title in caps.

Stat tile labels swapped from "BATTERY" / "RUNWAY" to "Low" / "Left" — sentence case, less business-card.

item.title: Version 1.2.8
item.description:
1.2.8

Menu polish, meeting forecast in the menu, redesigned Battery Health.

The menu-bar dropdown got context-aware about the time-remaining line. When a charge limit is set, it now reads "1h 45m until 85%" instead of the bare "1h 45m"; the now-redundant "Charging to 85%" segment drops out so the line stops repeating itself. On battery it reads "1h 45m left"; without a limit it reads "1h 45m until full". The lightning bolt next to the line is now a template image, so it tints white on dark menus and black on light menus the same way macOS's own menu glyphs do. The Pro badge in the menu header lifts ~2pt above the title baseline so it reads as a superscript flourish instead of hanging off the bottom.

A new meeting-forecast row sits directly below the status line whenever Calendar Battery Guard is enabled. Layout is [icon] Accent · body text at 10pt — the accent label is the only thing that picks up a colour. Severity → accent:

  • comfortable → green "Clear"
  • tight → orange "Tight"
  • critical → red "Charge"
  • catastrophic → red "Charge now"

Icon matches the accent (calendar.badge.checkmark / .clock / .exclamationmark). Body text stays in labelColor (white on dark, black on light) so the row doesn't saturate. When the guard is on but nothing's pending in the lookahead window, the row shows a green "Clear · No meetings in next 4h" confirmation. When the guard is off, the row hides entirely.

The Top Power-Hungry Apps panel gained a small info-circle next to its subtitle on the 24-hour and 7-day windows. On hover the system tooltip explains the coverage filter — "Only apps observed for most of the last 24 hours appear here, so percentages stay comparable across rows." The 1-hour view stays badge-less.

Battery Health got a full redesign. Each of the four tiles now leads with a tinted glyph in a soft tinted disc and stacks the value + kicker label beside it. Each metric carries its own colour band:

  • Capacity: green ≥85%, kin (gold) 75–84%, hinomaru <75%. Inline 3pt rail visualises 0–100%.
  • Cycles: neutral 0–600, kin 600–899, hinomaru ≥900 (against Apple's ~1000-cycle design target).
  • Temperature: aizome blue <10°C, neutral 10–34°C, kin 35–39°C, hinomaru ≥40°C.
  • Condition: green "Normal", hinomaru "Service" — the verdict text itself picks up the tint so the row reads at a glance.

Narrow layouts collapse to a 2×2 grid instead of a single column so the tiles keep a comfortable reading width.

The BATTERY · SENSEI title chrome stopped being translucent. The strip previously used .ultraThinMaterial, which let the hero card and parchment patina bleed through even at full opacity. The top of the chrome is now a solid theme fill — only the lower ~40% fades into the parchment below, so the title region no longer overlaps the content underneath it.

Marketing 1.2.7 → 1.2.8, build 48 → 49.

item.title: Version 1.2.9
item.description:
1.2.9

Calendar permission survives updates, and the coverage hint actually hovers.

The Calendar Battery Guard no longer asks for permission from scratch after a version update. When macOS resets the calendar TCC entry between versions — which it does in certain code-signing edge cases regardless of the app — the guard now detects the mismatch (was previously granted, current status reports notDetermined, guard still enabled) and re-requests automatically after launch settles. One system prompt appears, you click Allow, the guard is back. No more "off, on, oh I have to grant again" dance after every update.

Three guards layered to make sure prompts only fire when TCC genuinely doesn't know: requestAccess() re-reads the live authorization status at entry and short-circuits without calling EventKit at all if access is already granted. The init backfills the sticky "previously granted" flag for anyone whose grant predated this release. The auto re-prompt path itself re-checks status right before firing, so a grant during the 1-second settle window cancels the prompt instead of duplicating it.

The Top Power-Hungry Apps info-circle next to the 24-hour and 7-day subtitle finally responds to hover. The .help() tooltip on a bare SwiftUI Image doesn't always activate — the view isn't in the responder chain so macOS often doesn't deliver hover events. The badge is now a plain Button with a 4pt padded hit target, pointing-hand cursor on hover, a brighten on the glyph itself, and a click-to-open popover for trackpad-tap users who don't wait for tooltip dwell.

Marketing 1.2.8 → 1.2.9, build 49 → 50.

item.title: Version 1.2.10
item.description:
1.2.10

Faster auto-update propagation.

Sparkle's scheduled background check now runs every 7 hours instead of the 24-hour default. With the appcast already served from a CDN edge, the bandwidth cost of three checks a day per client is negligible; the win is that fixes and small improvements reach users within the same day instead of waiting up to a full 24-hour cycle.

Manual checks via Settings → "Check for updates now" still work the same way. Users who disable automatic checks see no behavioural change.

Marketing 1.2.9 → 1.2.10, build 50 → 51.

item.title: Version 1.2.11
item.description:
1.2.11

Cleaner, more natural wording in every language.

A full copy pass across English, German, Spanish, French, and Japanese. Each language was edited for native phrasing instead of literal translation, while the calm Sensei voice stays exactly the same. Setup, warnings, the Sensei Saga, and the licensing flow now read more like a person wrote them and less like a machine.

Along the way: brand terms stay consistent from screen to screen, a few clumsy phrasings and stray dashes are gone, and the Japanese share moments lean into the power-up theme.

No behaviour changes. Same features, clearer words.

Marketing 1.2.10 → 1.2.11, build 51 → 52.

item.title: Version 1.3.0
item.description:
1.3.0

Battery Sensei now reads naturally in every language.

The headline this release is a top-to-bottom rework of the app's wording across English, German, Spanish, French, and Japanese. Real native phrasing for each one, not literal translation, with the calm Sensei voice carried through. Setup, warnings, battery care, the Sensei Saga, and licensing all read like a person wrote them.

Also in 1.3.0:

  • Counts and plurals now follow each language's own rules
  • More reliable meeting battery guard: it recovers calendar access on launch if the system permission was reset

Warnings and charging behave exactly as before. Same Sensei, clearer words.

Marketing 1.2.11 → 1.3.0, build 52 → 53.

item.title: Version 1.4.0
item.description:
1.4.0

Keep your battery cooler, and see exactly where your power is going.

Pause charging when it's hot

Battery Sensei can now hold charging when the battery runs warm, then resume on its own once it cools. Lithium-ion ages faster when it's hot and full, so this takes the edge off the worst case. Pick a threshold — Off, 35°C, 40°C, or 45°C — in Battery Care or during setup. It steps aside automatically for Charge to Full and Travel Mode, and the menu bar shows a thermometer while a pause is active.

Live power flow

The Sensei Saga tab gains a Power Flow panel: what's coming in from the adapter, what your Mac is drawing, and whether the battery is charging or discharging — each with a clear label and direction, so the numbers finally line up with what's actually happening.

Quit power-hungry apps in place

The per-app energy detail now has a Quit button with a tidy progress-then-checkmark animation. If an app won't quit gracefully, you'll get an in-place Force Quit confirmation.

Smaller touches

  • Opening the window keeps you on the tab you last used instead of jumping to Today.
  • Running apps show a live green status dot in the energy list.

Warnings and charge-limit behavior are unchanged.

Marketing 1.3.0 → 1.4.0, build 53 → 54.

item.title: Version 1.5.0
item.description:
1.5.0

See what your Mac is actually doing, and trust the per-app power numbers more than ever.

Live system load graphs

The System load panel now opens into a detail view with live CPU, GPU, and disk I/O graphs over the last minute. CPU and GPU show load as a percentage; disk shows throughput in MB/s. You can see per-core CPU activity, GPU utilization channels, and the hardware behind the numbers — a clear picture of where the work is going moment to moment.

More honest per-app power

Per-app energy now uses direct process-energy counters when macOS exposes them, and falls back to activity-based estimates only when it can't measure a process directly. Each row is labeled Measured or Estimated from activity so you know which is which, and shows whether an app leans on the performance or efficiency cores.

A new Other measured processes row captures real per-process energy from helpers, agents, and background services that don't map to a visible app. System & hardware is now the measured whole-Mac power left after subtracting everything Sensei could attribute — not a rough guess.

Smaller touches

  • Clearer, shorter help text on the power panels explaining measured vs. estimated.

Warnings and charge-limit behavior are unchanged.

Marketing 1.4.0 → 1.5.0, build 54 → 55.

item.title: Version 1.5.1
item.description:
1.5.1

Memory joins the System load panel, the power-flow readout goes live, and a few rough edges get smoothed.

Memory in System load

The System load panel now shows Memory alongside CPU, GPU, and disk — a live RAM-used percentage with the same one-minute graph. Open it for an expandable breakdown: app, wired, and compressed memory, used vs. total, and swap in use. The CPU, GPU, disk, and memory detail breakdowns are now all collapsible.

Live power flow

The Power flow panel now refreshes every few seconds instead of only on charger changes, so adapter, system, and battery numbers track what your Mac is doing in real time. The System figure always reflects the true system load, and on battery the discharge reading shows the actual system draw.

Smaller touches

  • App energy detail: the "Measured · Performance-biased" tag now lives in the detail popover (not the compact rows), and the close button sits at the top-right.
  • Meeting Battery Guard re-forecasts immediately when you add, edit, or delete an event in Calendar.app.
  • Clearer Travel Mode summary copy.

Marketing 1.5.0 → 1.5.1, build 55 → 56.

item.title: Version 1.5.2
item.description:
1.5.2

Clearer per-app power in the live view, plus a tidier window.

Power numbers that add up

In the live Now view, the "Top power-hungry apps" list now always shows the System & hardware draw at the top and a remaining apps row at the bottom — not just when they happen to be large. Switch to percent and every row (apps, system, remaining) is shown as a share of the whole-Mac draw, so the list adds up to ~100%. The 3h and 5d views still report each app as a share of a full battery.

Smaller touches

  • The window now shows only the close button — the zoom and minimize buttons are gone.

Marketing 1.5.1 → 1.5.2, build 56 → 57.

item.title: Version 1.5.3
item.description:
1.5.3

Polish for the live power list.

Smaller touches

  • Fixed the leaderboard bars briefly overflowing when switching between the Now, 3h, and 5d windows.
  • The System & hardware row no longer draws a bar — just its value.
  • The live per-app share now shows one decimal of precision (e.g. 42.3%).

Marketing 1.5.2 → 1.5.3, build 57 → 58.

item.title: Version 1.5.4
item.description:
1.5.4

Small polish and refinements under the hood.

Marketing 1.5.3 → 1.5.4, build 58 → 59.

item.title: Version 1.5.5
item.description:
1.5.5

A cleaner menu-bar and dropdown, plus a few visual fixes.

Menu bar & dropdown

  • The menu-bar icon is calmer — no charging bolt cluttering the battery glyph (the charge-limit leaf and thermal indicator stay).
  • The dropdown status line leads with a battery icon and shows whichever of percentage / time the menu-bar icon isn't already showing, with the meeting forecast (icon + short word) right after.
  • The meeting forecast now lives inline on the status line, on battery only.

Smaller touches

  • Pro features are now marked with a badge next to each feature title.
  • Tidied the warnings control, app-language picker, and Meeting Battery Guard spacing.
  • App language now sits above Theme in General settings.

Marketing 1.5.4 → 1.5.5, build 59 → 60.

item.title: Version 1.6.0
item.description:
1.6.0

The menu-bar status indicators are back — now optional — on a steadier battery glyph.

Menu bar

  • New Show status indicators toggle in General settings: show or hide the symbols drawn inside the menu-bar battery — the charging bolt (light blue when plugged in, white while charging), the charge-limit leaf, and the temperature symbol. On by default.
  • The battery glyph now holds a steady width as the charge level changes and as indicators appear or disappear, so the menu bar stops shifting around. The reading is a lighter weight and centred, with the indicator tucked to its right.

Smaller touches

  • Launching Battery Sensei again while it's already running now reopens Settings.
  • Smoother app-power sampling and a few stability fixes under the hood.

Marketing 1.5.5 → 1.6.0, build 60 → 61.

item.title: Version 1.6.1
item.description:
1.6.1

Internal refactoring and a couple of small fixes.

Fixes

  • The meeting-alert Preview button now always shows the low-battery warning it's meant to demonstrate, even when your real next meeting would comfortably survive on the current charge.
  • Turning Show menu bar icon off now fades the dependent status-indicators row out cleanly before the layout collapses, instead of the row jumping as it disappeared. Turning it back on expands the space first, then fades the row in.

Under the hood

  • A large internal refactor: the app's central model was split into focused, independently-testable pieces (licensing, warnings, app-power, battery status, charging control, settings, saga), and the biggest source files were broken up. No behaviour change — purely structural, with added unit tests.

Marketing 1.6.0 → 1.6.1, build 61 → 62.

item.title: Version 1.6.2
item.description:
1.6.2

Menu bar polish and time-remaining fixes.

Fixes

  • The menu bar battery icon now keeps a fixed width — it no longer subtly resizes or jumps as the battery state changes, and its contents stay centered instead of overflowing the icon.
  • When plugged in but not actively charging (e.g. held at your charge limit), the menu bar now shows a clear power-plug glyph instead of a hard-to-see lightning bolt.
  • Time remaining menu bar mode is now strictly time-based: it never falls back to a percentage, shows the time until full while charging, holds the last estimate through the brief gaps where macOS reports none, and shows a "⋯" while the estimate is still being calculated instead of going blank.

Marketing 1.6.1 → 1.6.2, build 62 → 63.

item.title: Version 1.6.3
item.description:
1.6.3

Menu bar alignment and rescue receipt polish.

Fixes

  • The menu bar battery icon is now slightly narrower for a tidier fit, and its text sits perfectly centered — the percentage and time-remaining readouts no longer drift to different heights or sit low in the icon.
  • The Battery Rescue Receipt now auto-dismisses faster (after 3 seconds), but stays open as long as your pointer is hovering it — so it never vanishes mid-read.
  • The receipt's "Esc to close" keycap is now clearly legible against the receipt background.

Marketing 1.6.2 → 1.6.3, build 63 → 64.

item.title: Version 1.7.0
item.description:
1.7.0

Honors: your battery saves and care, turned into a collection — plus a tidier layout.

Honors & achievements

  • Every battery rescue is now kept as a browsable collection with its own context-aware story and an S/A/B/C grade — instead of only ever showing the latest one.
  • A new Honors collection of ~50 earnable seals lives in the Saga tab: rescues, healthy-charging streaks, longevity milestones, charging habits, records, and more — each a collectible seal ranked Bronze → Silver → Gold → Jade → Dragon.
  • Earning a seal shows a celebration that reveals a rotating 3D trophy, and you can share any seal. Locked seals appear as silhouettes with progress, so you can see what's next.
  • Records & streak band at a glance: closest call, fastest reflex, busiest day, current healthy streak, and seals earned.
  • Celebrations are never intrusive — they wait for a calm moment (e.g. right after you plug in) and there's a new "Achievement pop-ups" switch in General settings to turn them off entirely (seals are still tracked).
  • Tracking starts fresh with this update — achievements count what happens from here on, not your past history.

Layout

  • Today now shows your live monitoring — Power flow (above the quick actions), system load, charge over the last 24 hours, and top power-hungry apps — with the redundant wattage readout removed.
  • Saga leads with a combined Battery Health card: the metric tiles are always visible, and the care recommendations tuck into an expandable section. Statistics and the Honors collection now share one card.
  • Warnings leads with Meeting Battery Guard, decluttered — the set-once notification options (style, dismissal, titles) collapse behind a Notification settings disclosure.

Fixes & polish

  • Charge-history chart: the hover tooltip now sits in front of the crosshair line instead of behind it.
  • Full German, Spanish, French, and Japanese translations for everything new.

Marketing 1.6.3 → 1.7.0, build 64 → 65.

item.title: Version 1.7.1
item.description:
1.7.1

A new seal to chase and a calmer Battery Health card.

Honors & achievements

  • New Busy Bee seal (Jade): rescue your battery five times in a single day. The hive never rests.

Battery Health

  • The Temperature tile has been removed from the Battery Health card — it left three focused tiles: Capacity, Condition, and Cycles. Live temperature still appears on the Today screen.

Marketing 1.7.0 → 1.7.1, build 65 → 66.

item.title: Version 1.7.2
item.description:
1.7.2

Calmer pop-ups after a rescue.

Fixes & polish

  • The share card and an achievement pop-up no longer appear at the same time after you plug in — they now play one after another, with the share card first.
  • The post-rescue share card now appears only from time to time instead of on every single plug-in, so it stays a treat. It's context-aware: dramatic, clutch saves still pop right away, while everyday top-ups are shown at most about once a day. Every rescue is still recorded in Honors either way.

Marketing 1.7.1 → 1.7.2, build 66 → 67.

item.title: Version 1.7.3
item.description:
1.7.3

A sharper software-update experience.

Fixes & polish

  • The app icon shown in the software-update window is now full resolution instead of a low-resolution version. (Because the updater shows the currently-installed app's icon, the crisp icon appears when updating from this version onward.)

Marketing 1.7.2 → 1.7.3, build 67 → 68.

item.title: Version 1.7.4
item.description:
1.7.4

Fixes & polish

  • The Customize warnings section now carries a Pro badge, so it's clear at a glance that fine-tuning thresholds, styles, and timing is a Pro feature — consistent with the other Pro surfaces.

Marketing 1.7.3 → 1.7.4, build 68 → 69.

item.title: Version 1.8.0
item.description:
1.8.0

A calmer, more focused Today tab — live status up front, the knobs tucked into Settings.

Today, simplified

  • Today now leads with live status: the battery hero now carries temperature and live system load (CPU, GPU, memory, disk) together in one place, with the standalone "System load" card removed.
  • Pause warnings and Travel Mode are now two compact actions right in the hero, instead of two full-width rows.
  • Removed the redundant "Status / On battery" tile — the Power Flow panel already shows charging vs. discharging.
  • The old Quick actions card is gone; its controls moved to Settings (below).

Charging controls live in Settings

  • Optimised Battery Charging, your daily charge limit, and the pause-charging-when-hot heat guard now sit together in a single Charging section in Settings.
  • The charge-limit control is clearer: the redundant slider is gone (presets + the −/+ steppers remain), and the recommended cap is now stated plainly as "85% · Recommended" instead of a checkmark that looked like a second selection.
  • The heat guard collapses behind its own toggle, so it stays out of the way until you turn it on.

Honors

  • Fixed the stat chips and seal dates that could clip ("FASTEST REFL…", "Earned 10. J…") and tightened the label spacing so they read cleanly.

Fixes & polish

  • Re-running the Setup Wizard now has a clear close button and responds to Esc (the first-run wizard stays a deliberate flow).
  • Top power-hungry apps: the long tail of apps drawing under 0.1% now folds into a single expandable row instead of a wall of "0.0%".
  • The chart and app-list time-range switchers now share one consistent, clearly-tappable style.
  • The home Pro thank-you badge now retires a week after activation; your Pro status still lives in Settings → License.
  • Achievement pop-up and seal-detail buttons are now evenly sized.
  • Added an accessibility label to the charge-limit steppers, and full German, Spanish, French, and Japanese translations for everything new.

Marketing 1.7.4 → 1.8.0, build 69 → 70.

item.title: Version 1.8.1
item.description:
1.8.1

A quick follow-up polishing the new Today hero.

Polish

  • Today hero, tidied: the Pause warnings and Travel Mode actions now sit at the top, and the live system-load metrics (CPU, GPU, memory, disk) read as one compact, evenly-styled set with tighter labels. The battery-temperature tile was removed to cut clutter — it still drives the heat guard and warnings behind the scenes.
  • Honors: the stat chips (Seals, Closest Call, Fastest Reflex, Healthy Streak) no longer clip their labels on narrower windows.

Marketing 1.8.0 → 1.8.1, build 70 → 71.

item.title: Version 1.8.2
item.description:
1.8.2

Much lighter on the battery.

Performance

  • Fixed a significant background energy drain: the app's live animations (power-flow dots, the hero-ring shimmer, the wattage bar) kept rendering at full frame rate even while the window was closed, keeping the CPU busy continuously. They now pause whenever the window isn't on screen — idle CPU use with the window closed drops from ~30% to essentially zero.
  • The live system-load sampling now runs only while the window is open, instead of every few seconds around the clock.

Marketing 1.8.1 → 1.8.2, build 71 → 72.

item.title: Version 1.8.3
item.description:
1.8.3

A big battery and performance pass.

Performance

  • Major drop in background energy use. With the window closed, Battery Sensei now does almost nothing — idle CPU goes from roughly a third of a core down to near zero. The live animations, system‑load sampling, and recap recomputation all pause when you're not looking, instead of running around the clock.
  • Live animations are lighter (30fps) while the window is open.
  • The app now lets macOS throttle it while the display is asleep, and stays fully responsive whenever the screen is on (battery warnings are unaffected while you're using your Mac).

App Power

  • The per‑app detail chart now plots real watts (on Apple silicon) instead of an abstract impact score, so a power‑hungry app's curve clearly sits above a light one.

Today

  • The live system‑load strip now sits above the quick actions.

Marketing 1.8.2 → 1.8.3, build 72 → 73.

item.title: Version 1.8.4
item.description:
1.8.4

A polish release: more battery savings while the window is open, and a nicer achievement trophy.

Performance

  • Panels now pause when scrolled off‑screen. Animations like the power‑flow and the charge ring stop drawing once they scroll out of view and resume the moment they're back, so an open window costs less while you read further down.
  • Live readings appear faster after opening a panel instead of waiting for the first full sampling interval.
  • A broad reactivity overhaul under the hood — the app now updates only the views whose data actually changed, for lighter, smoother UI refreshes.

Achievements

  • The spinning 3D trophy is reframed with a flattering portrait‑style camera that looks slightly down onto the cup, so the whole trophy is shown instead of being clipped at the base.

Marketing 1.8.3 → 1.8.4, build 73 → 74.

item.title: Version 1.8.5
item.description:
1.8.5

A refinement release: the charge-limit control is simpler, small battery drainers are easier to tell apart, and achievement buttons get a brushed-metal look.

Charging

  • The charge-limit control is now a single, clearer row. The old percentage readout, plus/minus steppers, and the separate "recommended" caption have been folded into one tidy set of preset chips — with the Sensei-recommended cap marked right on its own chip. A short line explains what the cap actually does: charging pauses at your limit and resumes when the level dips below it.

App Power

  • Small battery drainers are easier to tell apart. In the 3-hour and 5-day views, apps that use less than 10% of a charge now show one decimal place, so a light background app reading "≈ 0.4%" no longer rounds to the same "≈ 1%" as something using three times more.

Interface

  • Achievement buttons get a flat brushed-metal look. Done and Share buttons on unlocked achievements now wear a matte metal "plate" finish tinted to the achievement's rank, with an angled sheen instead of a glossy 3D pill. Silver buttons were also darkened slightly so their labels stay readable.
  • More buttons respond to hover and clicks. Celebration buttons, the birthday-cake copy and close buttons, the setup-wizard close button, and other controls that previously felt static now give proper press and hover feedback.
  • Setup wizard cleanup. The step markers are flatter and calmer (no more 3D glow), the progress-and-permissions screen reads more concisely, and the permissions explanations are tightened to the essentials.
  • Dismissing a warning overlay is snappier. Closing a warning by hand (Escape or the dismiss button) now fades out quickly instead of using the slow, cinematic fade reserved for the charging celebration.
  • Menu-bar hint is simpler. The pop-up that points at the menu bar dropped a small decorative stamp for a cleaner arrow.

Marketing 1.8.4 → 1.8.5, build 74 → 75.

item.title: Version 1.8.6
item.description:
1.8.6

A quality release: achievement celebrations now wait for a fitting moment instead of interrupting you, plus a large under-the-hood tidy-up.

Achievements

  • Unlock celebrations no longer pop up at bad moments. A newly-earned seal used to appear after a brief lull in activity — which is exactly when you're watching a full-screen video, presenting slides, or on a call. Celebrations now hold back while you're in a full-screen app, on camera or mic, in a calendar meeting, or your screen is locked, and instead wait for a natural breather. Plugging in still celebrates a fresh charging or rescue seal right away, unless you're mid-presentation or on a call.
  • A celebration that never found a good moment stops trying. If a seal has waited a couple of days without a fitting time to appear, it quietly retires to the Honors gallery with its "new" badge instead of surfacing as stale news.

Under the hood

  • Large internal reorganization. The source tree was regrouped into per-feature folders and several oversized files were split along single responsibilities, with tests moved alongside the logic they cover. No behavior change — this keeps the codebase healthy for future work.

Marketing 1.8.5 → 1.8.6, build 75 → 76.

item.title: Version 1.9.0
item.description:
1.9.0

Per-app battery numbers now tell the whole story: an app's helpers and everything it launches count toward that app.

App power attribution

  • Apps now own the battery cost of everything they spawn. Browsers, editors, and AI tools do most of their work in helper and child processes — a browser tab renderer, a compiler kicked off by your IDE, a shell command run by an assistant. Those used to hide in an anonymous "other processes" bucket; now they're attributed to the app that launched them, the same way Activity Monitor groups its Energy pane.
  • Helper processes no longer clutter the list as separate entries. Entries like "Steam Helper" or "Discord Helper (Renderer)" fold into their parent app, so the leaderboard shows apps you recognize instead of plumbing.
  • The unattributed remainder shrinks dramatically. With helpers rolled up, nearly all measured process power lands on a named app, making the per-app breakdown far more honest about who's actually draining your battery.

Marketing 1.8.6 → 1.9.0, build 76 → 77.

item.title: Version 1.9.1
item.description:
1.9.1

Today feels light and responsive again, with clearer Travel Mode guidance and more reliable background monitoring.

Performance

  • The Today screen stays smooth while Battery Sensei works. System-load sampling, calendar lookups, history preparation, achievement progress, and other heavier calculations no longer compete with drawing and interaction on the main UI thread.
  • The battery shimmer keeps its familiar 60 fps motion with much less rendering work. Its timing, soft falloff, translucent gold stroke, and bristled edges retain the established hand-painted character.
  • App Power monitoring does less repeated work. Process ownership and running-app information are reused between samples, while history stores only the data needed to reconstruct the charts.

Today

  • Travel Mode now explains itself. A dedicated info button describes what the temporary 100% charge does, when it ends, and how your normal charge and heat settings return afterward.
  • The hero layout has a calmer rhythm. The title, system-load metrics, warning control, and Travel Mode action are grouped and spaced more clearly.

Reliability

  • Recent history is safer during launch and quit. Battery and App Power storage now guard against delayed loads overwriting fresh samples, debounce background saves, and flush pending changes when the app closes.
  • Calendar refreshes cannot replace newer results with stale ones. Meeting checks run away from the UI and discard superseded queries.
  • Achievement progress persists consistently. Newly calculated progress is saved alongside unlock state instead of being recomputed and forgotten between launches.

Marketing 1.9.0 → 1.9.1, build 77 → 78.

item.title: Version 1.10.0
item.description:
1.10.0

Power handoffs are instant, nearby devices read over Bluetooth, and every alert can carry its own sound — with a calmer, more consistent layout throughout.

Power handoffs

  • The plug-in estimate appears the moment you connect. Battery Sensei remembers your charger's rate — even across launches — so it shows time-to-full right away instead of waiting for the charge to settle, then quietly refines it. No more loading spinner.
  • Unplug estimates use your last ten minutes of usage. The runtime shown when you disconnect is steadier and more realistic, rather than reacting to a momentary spike.
  • Charging time counts down to your charge limit, not to 100%. At 84% with an 85% limit it now reads a minute or two, not hours; holding at the limit shows no phantom countdown.

Devices

  • See nearby iPhone and iPad battery over Bluetooth. An opt-in in Warnings and the setup wizard — turning it on is the only time Battery Sensei asks for Bluetooth permission, and it's off until you do. Accessories like AirPods and mice keep working as before.

Alerts

  • Give each alert its own sound. Low-battery warnings, the unplug and plug-in updates, and every custom warning rule can chime with a fitting sound — or stay silent, which is the default. Picking a sound previews it instantly.
  • Redesigned overlays. The plug-in, unplug, and low-battery windows now use a clean, iconic battery that fills to your level, animates, and shows a fuller bar when critically low. The meeting forecast reads more concisely.

Settings & setup

  • A tidier General screen. The app version and update controls share one panel, "Pro is active" and the About footer line up cleanly, and everything about the menu bar lives under one heading.
  • Warnings, together. The device switcher sits under the Warnings title, and the plug/unplug updates are a connected section rather than a separate card.
  • A refreshed setup wizard. It fits its own height when it opens, drops a duplicate close button, shows your devices, and groups update checks with the other system settings.

Marketing 1.9.1 → 1.10.0, build 78 → 79.

item.title: Version 1.10.1
item.description:
1.10.1

Third-party device alerts now match the Mac's in full, warning overlays show how much time you have left, and the alert layouts are calmer and more consistent throughout.

Devices

  • Accessory alerts are now fully configurable. Low-battery alerts for AirPods, mice, and other devices get the same controls as the Mac's own warnings — warning style, manual or auto-close dismissal, close timing, and a per-alert sound. The editor mirrors the Mac's custom-warning design so it feels identical to set up.
  • Preview each device rule in place. A Test button sits at the top of every device alert card, previewing that rule's exact style, sound, and timing.

Alerts

  • See how much time you have left. Low-battery and meeting warnings now show an estimated runtime — "About 1h 20m of battery left" — right under the readout, on the Mac where the estimate is reliable.
  • A clearer entrance. When a battery alert appears, its battery visibly drains once to your current level, so the drop reads at a glance.
  • Calmer, more consistent overlays. The hero icon, the title-and-percentage readout, and the buttons now share one rhythm across every alert style. Device alerts drop the redundant "battery has dropped to X%" line — the title and the big number already say it.
  • Give each alert its own sound. Per-rule and meeting-guard sounds are easier to set, sit in the same place in every editor, and switch instantly.

Consistency

  • Preview buttons live in one place. Every alert — Mac rules, device rules, and the meeting guard — puts its Test/Preview button at the top of the card, the same way.
  • Tidier power handoffs. The Unplug and Plug-in update icons now sit beside their titles instead of floating in the middle of the row.

Marketing 1.10.0 → 1.10.1, build 79 → 80.

item.title: Version 1.10.2
item.description:
1.10.2

Battery Sensei now practices what it preaches: with the window open, the app's own energy use drops from a steady hum to almost nothing. The app also stays responsive when macOS's own power services stall, and plug-in alerts react the moment you connect.

Performance

  • The open window no longer costs you battery. The power-flow dots and the battery ring's shimmer are now drawn by the system's animation engine instead of being recomputed by the app every frame. CPU use with the window open and focused drops from a constant double-digit load to near zero, with only brief activity while the shimmer sweeps.
  • Fewer background wakeups. Accessory battery checks run half as often (opening the menu still refreshes instantly), and per-app power attribution and system-load telemetry stop re-asking the kernel for answers that cannot change.
  • Lighter periodic work. Achievement progress is evaluated less eagerly, and history lookups scan only the window they need instead of the whole store.

Reliability

  • No more freezes when macOS's power services stall. Calls into the system's charging and Low Power Mode services are synchronous, so a service that stopped answering could hold up the app. Those calls are now bounded by a deadline and back off briefly after a timeout, so the interface keeps responding and recovers on its own.

Alerts

  • Plug-in feedback is immediate. The charge panel now appears the moment you connect, showing its estimating state while macOS negotiates charge current, then filling in the estimate once telemetry lands — instead of staying blank through the ramp.
  • Battery fills settle naturally. Level animations decelerate into place rather than stopping abruptly.
  • Sounds follow the alert. Warning sounds are configured per alert rather than as one global setting, so each rule plays what you chose for it.

Fixes

  • The window remembers its size again. Reopening the window now restores your exact saved size and position; fresh installs open at the intended default size instead of the minimum.

Polish

  • External links look like links. Every button that leaves the app — buy, manage subscription, system-settings shortcuts — now shares one consistent link style.

Marketing 1.10.1 → 1.10.2, build 80 → 82.

item.title: Version 1.10.3
item.description:
1.10.3

A follow-up to 1.10.2: the app-power list tells the truth again, and Low Power Mode repairs itself instead of stalling.

App power

  • Your apps are back in the list. The "Now" list could collapse into a single "14 apps under 0.02 W" row, hiding real apps. An app whose live reading had not arrived yet was being treated as though it were drawing nothing — so it was filed away as negligible. A missing reading now means "unknown", never "zero", and the list keeps showing the app.
  • The numbers are watts again. Rows could show a bare three-digit number under "drawing now" — an activity score, not a wattage. Each row's value and its caption are now decided together, so they can never disagree; a row with no reading shows "—" rather than a number in the wrong unit.
  • Percentages make sense. In percent mode an app's share is measured against the power the apps are drawing, as the panel has always described it — instead of being diluted by the display and other hardware, which made a busy browser read a fraction of a percent. The menu bar's top-apps list now agrees with the panel.
  • Small apps are summarised, not swallowed. The collapsed row now shows the group's combined draw, so the numbers on screen add up, and it never hides an app you searched for.

Low Power Mode

  • It fixes itself. If the helper stops responding — after the app is moved, restored from a backup, or migrated to a new Mac — Battery Sensei now repairs its own registration instead of waiting and then failing. If it needs your approval, it says so plainly rather than doing nothing.
  • The switch updates instantly. Turning Low Power Mode on or off now updates the menu and the button immediately, instead of showing the previous state for a few seconds.

Marketing 1.10.2 → 1.10.3, build 82 → 83.

item.title: Version 1.10.4
item.description:
1.10.4

The time-remaining estimate settles down: it stops lurching when your workload spikes, and corrects itself gently instead of jumping.

Time remaining

  • A steadier estimate. Battery time was reading straight off instantaneous draw, so a brief CPU burst or a bright display could swing it wildly. Readings are now smoothed, outliers are rejected, and the estimate leans on the whole-system readings Sensei already collects — no extra polling, no extra battery cost.
  • No more jumps when it learns more. As Sensei moves from a cached estimate to live telemetry, the displayed time now eases toward the truth — correcting by at most 45 minutes per minute — instead of snapping to a new number.
  • The right direction, always. Whether the Mac is charging or discharging is now decided by the power source itself, so a contradictory sensor reading can no longer flip the estimate the wrong way. A pack sitting at its charge limit reads as holding, not charging.
  • An estimate the moment you unplug. Recent background readings seed the number immediately, so it is useful straight away rather than after a warm-up.

Marketing 1.10.3 → 1.10.4, build 83 → 84.

item.title: Version 1.11.0
item.description:
1.11.0

Meeting Battery Guard grows up: forecasts you can trust, a real full-screen alert with keyboard control, and a Low Power Mode remedy on every warning.

Meeting Battery Guard

  • Forecasts that match reality. The prediction no longer bills the waiting time before a meeting at video-call drain: only the meeting itself runs at the elevated rate, and that boost now adapts to how close the meeting is and how hard your Mac is already working. A battery that comfortably outlasts your event no longer cries "thin margin".
  • The alert you configured actually appears. Critical forecasts now present your chosen alert style live — full-screen included — not just in the Settings preview. Each meeting alerts once: later reminders stay quiet banners, and a snooze brings the alert back after exactly the time you chose.
  • Honest wording. A battery that survives to the start but not the end now says "dies before your meeting ends" instead of claiming it won't reach the start.
  • A 2-hour lookahead. Forecasts further out were too uncertain to act on; the guard now watches the window where its advice is dependable.

Warnings

  • Low Power Mode, one tap away. Every battery and meeting alert now offers "Low Power Mode" beside snooze — the remedy for the moments you can't reach a charger. Low Power Mode also wears a new tortoise icon everywhere, so the leaf now always means charge care.
  • Keyboard control. Esc dismisses, F1 snoozes, F2 turns on Low Power Mode, and + / − adjust the snooze time — from any app, with the shortcuts printed right on the buttons.
  • Alerts that stay out of your way. Full-screen warnings no longer trap your clicks: the tinted wash lets you keep working underneath, and compact alerts intercept the pointer only where the card actually is.

Today & menu bar

  • A calmer hero. The Today card leads with the app identity, the enso ring now carries your percentage at its centre, and system load moved to its own section beside the app power list.
  • System load in the menu — if you want it. An opt-in line adds live CPU, GPU, memory, and disk readings to the menu, measured only while the menu is open. The new "Menu content" settings group collects everything the dropdown shows.

Collection & health

  • A tidier Honors wall. The seal gallery opens at three rows with a "Show all" capsule — earned seals lead.
  • All good means all good. Battery health recommendations show a green checkmark when everything is a confirmation, instead of counting them like open tasks.

Marketing 1.10.4 → 1.11.0, build 84 → 85.
